title: Nutrigenomics in Dairy Cattle: Causes and Implications.
one_liner_zh: 该文综述奶牛营养基因组学，探讨营养素与基因表达及表观遗传的互作，未涉及三维基因组、染色质组织或空间架构建模，且无AI/分子模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Nutrigenomics is a rapidly developing interdisciplinary field that investigates the interactions between nutrients and the genome, with particular emphasis on how dietary components regulate gene expression and metabolic pathways. In dairy cattle, nutrigenomics has gained increasing attention due to its potential to improve milk production, metabolic efficiency, health, reproduction, and overall animal performance. Nutrients and bioactive dietary compounds can influence gene activity directly through transcriptional regulation or indirectly through epigenetic mechanisms such as DNA methylation, histone modification, and noncoding RNA-mediated gene regulation. These nutrigenomic interactions affect important biological processes including lipid metabolism, adipogenesis, immune response, mammary gland development, and milk synthesis. Advances in omics technologies including transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and next-generation sequencing have enhanced understanding of the molecular responses of dairy cows to nutritional interventions. Dietary fatty acids, vitamins, methyl donors, and short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate have been shown to regulate key transcription factors including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), sterol regulatory element binding proteins (SREBPs), and liver X receptors (LXRs), thereby modulating metabolic and physiological functions. Nutritional interventions, feed restriction, and supplementation produce tissue-specific molecular responses in the liver, adipose tissue, mammary gland, and immune system, demonstrating interaction between diet, physiological state, and metabolic regulation. Despite these advances, challenges with genetic and physiological variability, tissue-specific responses, integration of multi-omics data, and translation of molecular findings into practical feeding strategies remain unresolved. Future integration of nutrigenomics with microbiome research, multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and precision livestock technologies may facilitate nutritional strategies to improve dairy cattle health, productivity, feed efficiency, and product quality.
abstract_zh: 营养基因组学是一个快速发展的跨学科领域，研究营养素与基因组之间的相互作用，特别关注膳食成分如何调控基因表达和代谢通路。在奶牛中，营养基因组学因其在改善产奶性能、代谢效率、健康、繁殖及整体动物表现方面的潜力而日益受到关注。营养素和具有生物活性的膳食化合物可通过转录调控直接影响基因活性，或通过表观遗传机制（如DNA甲基化、组蛋白修饰和非编码RNA介导的基因调控）间接发挥作用。这些营养基因组学相互作用影响重要的生物学过程，包括脂质代谢、脂肪生成、免疫应答、乳腺发育和乳合成。转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学和下一代测序等组学技术的进步增强了对奶牛营养干预分子反应的理解。膳食脂肪酸、维生素、甲基供体和短链脂肪酸（如丁酸）已被证明可调控关键转录因子，包括过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARs）、固醇调节元件结合蛋白（SREBPs）和肝X受体（LXRs），从而调节代谢和生理功能。营养干预、限饲和补充剂在肝脏、脂肪组织、乳腺和免疫系统中产生组织特异性分子反应，展示了饮食、生理状态和代谢调控之间的相互作用。尽管有这些进展，遗传和生理变异性、组织特异性反应、多组学数据整合以及将分子发现转化为实际饲喂策略等方面的挑战仍未解决。未来将营养基因组学与微生物组研究、多组学、人工智能和精准畜牧业技术相结合，可能有助于制定改善奶牛健康、生产力、饲料效率和产品品质的营养策略。
